questions.question: In ancient times the area to the south of the_____ river was known as Magadha.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ganga**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Magadha**:-

 
 
• **It was a powerful kingdom in ancient India, located in what is now the state of Bihar.**
 
• It was the birthplace of Buddhism and Jainism, and it played an important role in the development of Indian culture and civilization.
 
• **Magadha was known for its fertile soil, its strategic location on the Ganges River, and its rich mineral resources. **
 
• These factors contributed to its rise as a major power in ancient India. 
 
• **Magadha reached its peak under the Mauryan dynasty (322-184 BCE), which ruled over most of the Indian subcontinent.**
 
• The Mauryan Empire was one of the largest and most powerful empires in the ancient world.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ganga:-**

 
 
• **It is the largest and most sacred river in India. **
 
• It flows for over 2,500 km through the states of Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, and Odisha.
 
• The Ganga is revered by Hindus and is considered to be a holy river.
 
 
 
• **Yamuna:-**
 
 
• The Yamuna River is the **largest tributary of the Ganga.**
 
• It flows for approximately 1,376 km through **Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan.**
 
• The Yamuna is a major water source for drinking and irrigation, particularly in northern India.
 
 
 
• **Tapti:-**
 
 
• **It is a river that flows for over 700 km through the states of Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli. **
 
• The Tapti is a major source of water for drinking and irrigation, and it is also used for navigation.
 
 
 
• **Narmada:-**
 
 
• **It is a river that flows for over 1,300 km through the states of Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, and Maharashtra. **
 
• The Narmada is a major source of water for drinking and irrigation, and it is also used for navigation.

questions.question: In the game of football, the distance between the goalposts is _________ whereas the distance from the lower edge of the crossbar to the ground is _________.

• **It is also known as association football or soccer, is a team sport played between two teams of 11 players with a spherical ball. **
 
• It is played by 250 million players in over 200 countries and dependencies, making it the world's most popular sport.
 
• **In the game of football (also known as soccer), the distance between the goalposts is 7.32 meters (24 feet), and the distance from the lower edge of the crossbar to the ground is 2.44 meters (8 feet). **
 
• **These dimensions are specified in Law 1 of the Laws of the Game, which is published by the Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA).**
 
• The goalposts and crossbar must be made of wood, metal, or other approved material.
 
• They must be square, rectangular, round, or elliptical in shape, and they must not be dangerous to players. The goalposts and crossbar must also be white.

questions.question: Identify the local name given to the total amount of winter precipitation.
questions.solution:

__
 
• Low-pressure systems that originate over the Mediterranean Sea are known as western cyclonic disturbances.
 
• These wind systems go to India under the control of subtropical westerly jet streams, where they produce precipitation.
 
• The plains get these winter rains, which aid in the development of Rabi crops.
 
• Locally, this downpour is known as mahawat. It occurs in the northern and northwest regions of India.
 
• Westerly winds with high speed are called jet streams. The western disturbances felt in the country's north and north-western regions are caused by the westerly flows. Westerly jet streams flow to the Himalayan region's north in the summer.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Kaal Baisakhi
 
 
• ​It is a local rainfall and thunderstorm occur in Assam and West Bengal and in India or Bangladesh.
 
 
• It occurs in the summer season.
 
 
 
• It harms life and money and generally occurs in the month of Baisakh (April-May), hence it is known as 'Kaal Baisakhi'.
 
• It originated from Chota Nagpur Plateau.
 
• Since It is caused by winds coming from the north-west direction, they are also called 'norwesters'.​​
 
 
 
 
 
• **​Loo**

The Imperial Bank had the status of a quasi-central bank, undertaking until the formation of the Reserve Bank of India in 1935, banking functions for the Government of India and other banking institutions and managing the rupee debt of the government.

questions.question: In the post-independence period, who won the 1st individual Olympic Medal for India in 1952?

• **Jadhav is best known for winning a bronze medal at the 1952 Summer Olympics in Helsinki, Finland. He was the first athlete from independent India to win an individual medal in the Olympics. **

questions.question:

__
 
• **Bhil Tribe:-**

 
 
• The Bhils are one of the largest tribal groups in India.
 
• **They are traditionally hunters and gatherers, but many Bhils now practice agriculture.**
 
• The Bhils' control of the mountain passes between the north and the Deccan gave them a strategic advantage.
 
• They were able to levy tolls on merchants and travelers, and they could also use the passes to defend their territory.
 
• **The Bhil tribe living in the Western Ghats controlled the mountain passes between the north and the Deccan. **

• The Western Ghats are a mountain range that runs along the western coast of India.
 
• They form a natural barrier between the Deccan Plateau to the east and the Arabian Sea to the west.

• it talks about the office of the Attorney General of India.
 
• Attorney General of India is part of the Union Executive of India. AG is the highest law officer of India.

• AG is not considered a government servant.

questions.question: What is the number of electrons found in the outermost shell of the halogens?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seven**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Halogens:-**

 
 
• **These are a group of chemical elements that belong to group 17 of the periodic table. **
 
• They are highly reactive non-metals and are found in nature as diatomic molecules. The halogens are fluorine (F), chlorine (Cl), bromine (Br), iodine (I), and astatine (At).
 
• **All halogens have 7 electrons in their outermost shell.**
 
• The number of electrons in the outermost shell of an atom is called its valence electron count.
 
• **The valence electron count determines the chemical properties of an element. **
 
• Halogens have 7 valence electrons, which makes them very reactive. They tend to gain one electron to complete their octet (a stable configuration of 8 electrons in the outermost shell).

questions.question: Which among the following dance forms is not associated with Chhattisgarh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhagoria**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhagoria:-**

 
 
• **It is a tribal festival celebrated in the Indian states of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra. It is primarily celebrated by the Bhil, Bhilala, and Pateliya tribes. **
 
• The festival takes place in the Barwani, Dhar, Alirajpur, Khargone, and Jhabua districts of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.
 
• It has agricultural significance and coincides with the end of harvesting of crops. It is celebrated for seven days in the month of March before the Holi Festival.
 
• Bhagoria is a unique festival that celebrates love and marriage.
 
• It is a time for young men and women to meet and choose their partners. The festival is also a celebration of tribal culture and traditions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pandwani:-**

 
 
• **It is a folk singing style involving narration of tales from the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata. **
 
• The singing also involves musical accompaniment. Bhima, the second of the Pandava is the hero of the story in this style.
 
• Pandavani is a style of folk singing which includes narration of tales from the Mahabharata. While popular in Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Orissa, this form of folk theatre is predominantly performed in Chhattisgarh.
 
 
 
• **Saila**:-
 
 
• **It is a folk dance of India that is performed by the Bhil, Bhilala, and Pateliya tribes of the central Indian states of Madhya Pradesh and Chattisgarh. **
 
• The dance is a celebration of life and love, and it is often performed at weddings and other festive occasions.
 
 
 
• **Panthi:-**
 
 
• **Panthi Dance,** Folk Dance of Chhattisgarh is one of the important dance forms of **Chhattisgarh **State of India.
 
• It is primarily performed by tribal communities, especially the Bhil, Bhilala, and Pateliya tribes.
 
• Panthi dance originated in the Hoshangabad district of Madhya Pradesh, and it began as a religious ritual. However, over time, it evolved into a folk dance form.
